name: Traffic Operations Center
one_liner: A live SUMO digital twin of Oakland, Pittsburgh (and a 3x3 grid) where a camera-detected crash triggers candidate responses that are simulated in parallel branches before an agent (Nemotron, Claude or a rule-based mock) recommends, applies and learns from one.
judge_note: A live traffic digital twin of Oakland where a crash triggers parallel simulations of signal, EMS and detour plans before one is recommended and applied. wow_moment: Click 'Inject collision' on Forbes Avenue, watch the queue spill back on a live map of Oakland, then see nine alternative futures simulated in parallel and one EMS green corridor recommended with minutes saved.

evidence.one_liner: A live SUMO digital twin of Oakland, Pittsburgh (and a 3x3 grid) where a camera-detected crash triggers candidate responses that are simulated in parallel branches before an agent (Nemotron, Claude or a rule-based mock) recommends, applies and learns from one.
evidence.problem: Traffic operators respond to incidents by guesswork; signal retiming, EMS green corridors and diversions should be tested in simulation before being pushed to the street.
evidence.target_user: City traffic operations centers / incident managers (NVIDIA Smart City blueprint audience).
stack: Nemotron via NIM chat completions with tool calling

The only NVIDIA/Toyota/HackUTD mention is docs/hackathon-reference-projects.md, a ChatGPT-style list of other teams' projects (Toyotron etc.) used as inspiration; nothing in the tree derives from them. Git starts Sept 19 09:28 (2-line README), brainstorm at 09:59, then one 87-file, 10,270-line 'milestone 1' commit at 12:12, about one hour after hacking start; either pre-hackathon preparation or bulk agent generation, and the repo alone cannot distinguish. evidence.wow_moment: Click 'Inject collision' on Forbes Avenue, watch the queue spill back on a live map of Oakland, then see nine alternative futures simulated in parallel and one EMS green corridor recommended with minutes saved.

Gorgeous console and a big idea; the AI analyst (Nemotron) exists but was never actually run, so what judges see is probably the rule-based mock.

name: Stockd
one_liner: Barcode-scan inventory tracker and cold-start demand predictor for small food businesses: a brand-new shop gets a day-one forecast borrowed from peer shops, blended toward its own data as history accrues, with reorder and expiry actions. No language model anywhere.
judge_note: A no-LLM inventory forecaster for small restaurants that gives a new shop a day-one prediction from peer shops and blends toward its own scans over time. Polished, tested, phone-scannable, with a slider that shows the blend happening.
wow_moment: Drag the 'what if it only had N days of history' slider from 84 to 0 and watch the forecast line swing from the shop's own data onto the peer prior; then scan a barcode off the laptop screen with a phone and see stock and stats move.

evidence.one_liner: Barcode-scan inventory tracker and cold-start demand predictor for small food businesses: a brand-new shop gets a day-one forecast borrowed from peer shops, blended toward its own data as history accrues, with reorder and expiry actions. No language model anywhere.
evidence.problem: Independent restaurants run out on busy game days and throw away expired stock; existing forecasting tools need months of sales history before they say anything useful.
evidence.target_user: Owners of small independent food businesses (pizzerias, taquerias, cafes), especially newly opened ones.
stack: better-sqlite3 (persisted to MongoDB Atlas or Postgres on Vercel)
evidence.core_loop: Phone camera scans EAN-13 -> /api/scan -> lots with expiry (FEFO) -> forecast.ts: EWMA level x weekday profile x event multiplier (Pitt/Steelers games, holidays, exams, own deals) for own history, median size-normalized peer prior, blended w = n/(n+14) -> reorder list with safety stock and case rounding, 'use it or donate it' list for lots expiring before demand consumes them -> dashboard widgets and /stats live counters; onboarding a new shop by name/type/seats/ZIP yields an immediate peer-based forecast; CSV import, checklist, events calendar, plain-English product lookup (rule-based).
evidence.mocked_or_hardcoded: All data synthetic (five peer shops, 12 weeks of demo usage, fake barcodes) generated by scripts/seed.ts; event multipliers are fixed estimates; donation partners are placeholders; catalog lookup hits Open Food Facts / Open Library live. Backtest (11-16% MAPE) is on synthetic peers generated by the same process, which the README states plainly.
evidence.demo_risks: Low: runs fully offline with SQLite; camera needs HTTPS or localhost (dev:https and tunnel instructions provided); Vercel copy persists to Mongo/Postgres. Seed must be re-run the morning of the demo so events line up (documented).
evidence.ui_experience: Custom design with a 'kitchen ticket' motif (torn paper slips on a rail for event days), Bricolage Grotesque headings, basil/tomato/cheese palette, customizable widget dashboard, forecast chart with a what-if 'days of history' slider and own-vs-peer source bar, phone scanner page, products table with natural-language filter chips, calendar view, CSV import preview. Roughly 20 routes. Attractive and interactive.
evidence.integrity_flags: First three commits ('Stockd Team', 16:22-16:40 EDT on 9/19) land ~7k lines in 15 minutes, and COMMIT_GUIDE.md instructs teammates to unzip 'stockd-features.zip' and commit 7 features in 9 commits, so most code was generated outside the repo (within the event window) and pushed in bulk. README demo-video/slides/Devpost placeholders unfilled.
evidence.ai_scaffolding_flags: No CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md; COMMIT_GUIDE.md and DEPLOY docs read like agent output. Docs (~480 lines) are small next to ~10k lines of code and tests.
evidence.novelty_notes: Inventory management is a crowded category; the cold-start peer prior with an explicit blend weight, local event calendar and expiry-aware waste routing is a distinctive, well-explained mechanism.
evidence.need_notes: Specific user with a real two-sided loss (stockouts vs waste); argument is credible and the README is candid about synthetic evidence, but no operator interviews or real data.
evidence.wow_moment: Drag the 'what if it only had N days of history' slider from 84 to 0 and watch the forecast line swing from the shop's own data onto the peer prior; then scan a barcode off the laptop screen with a phone and see stock and stats move.
evidence.score_rationale: Nails No Wrapper (explicit no-LLM, explainable statistics, backtest, unit tests) and credibly stacks with Compound. Very complete, deployable, with a distinctive interactive chart and phone scanning. Novelty is moderate and all evidence is synthetic; bulk-pushed generated code is worth a look.
evidence.judge_summary: A no-LLM inventory forecaster for small restaurants that gives a new shop a day-one prediction from peer shops and blends toward its own scans over time. Polished, tested, phone-scannable, with a slider that shows the blend happening.

evidence.ai_scaffolding_flags: Large .agents/skills and .claude/skills trees (thousands of lines, shipped by the scaffold); docs/plans/voice-line.md is written as milestone tasks 'sized for one coding-agent task' with ADRs; CONTEXT.md glossary. Code (~12k lines TS) still outweighs docs.
evidence.novelty_notes: Voice-first, no-app banking for seniors with proactive outbound calls, PIN gating on both directions, permission tiers (instant / notify / needs approval) and a safe-to-spend number is a thoughtful twist on the fintech-for-families category.

evidence.wow_moment: Caretaker clicks 'inject $400 gift-card charge' on the dashboard, and a phone on the table rings: June greets Dot by name, asks for her PIN, then warns about the charge.

evidence.judge_summary: A voice agent seniors can phone about their money, with a caretaker dashboard that approves changes and injects fraud scenarios live. Big, well-structured build; the demo lands or dies on the phone call actually connecting.

evidence.ai_scaffolding_flags: DEMO.md runbook and a long README; no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md. Docs proportionate to ~5K lines of code.
evidence.novelty_notes: BEC callback automation is an uncommon hackathon problem; the design insight that holding is policy while the score only sets urgency (score catches 0/8 compromised-mailbox cases yet none escape) is a genuinely thought-through mechanism.
evidence.need_notes: BEC is a well-documented multi-billion-dollar fraud class; persona and cost framing (false positive = 2-minute call) show domain understanding; still no external user quotes.
evidence.wow_moment: The presenter hands a judge the mic, the judge says 'no, we never sent that', and the payment flips to BLOCKED on the judge's own voice with the transcript and verdict on screen.

judge_note: A very complete, live meal-plan tracker for ten schools with on-device receipt OCR and a Monte Carlo run-out forecast. Solid No Wrapper entry; not flashy. Note several feature commits landed ~90 minutes before the official start.
wow_moment: Photograph a real thermal receipt on your phone and it logs '1 block + $2.75 FLEX' at the right cafe, then the home screen says 'FLEX: over 99% chance of running out, Nov 6-17'.

evidence.one_liner: Track meal blocks/FLEX/dining dollars at 10 schools, scan receipts on-device, and get a Monte Carlo verdict on whether you'll run out before the semester ends.
evidence.problem: Dining apps show a balance but never whether it is enough; a $4k CMU plan is two currencies with different rules, so students either ration or hand $300 back in December.
evidence.target_user: College students on institutional meal plans (CMU, Pitt, Penn State, Temple, Penn, Drexel, Duquesne, Villanova, Lehigh, Rutgers).
evidence.core_loop: Pick school/plan (catalog from official pages with break calendars) -> log purchase by form, receipt photo (Tesseract + tender-line parser) or pasted Grubhub email -> localStorage or Supabase row -> per-bucket verdict, 2,000-run Monte Carlo band, today's meal-period plan, spend-by-place insights, plan advisor.
evidence.mocked_or_hardcoded: Sample-data generator (?demo) for judges; plan catalog hand-transcribed; Claude vision path present but switched off (DEFAULT_PROXY empty); CMU live hours from ScottyLabs API, other schools fixed lists; block values 'learned' only from receipts you feed it.
evidence.demo_risks: Low: static site works offline. Tesseract (~10 MB) loads from CDN on first scan and misreads crumpled receipts (results flagged 'check this'); Supabase sign-in and ScottyLabs API need network.
evidence.ui_experience: Four-tab dashboard (Home/Log/Eat/Plans) with school-colored badges, light/dark tokens, Chart.js actual/projected/ideal lines with shaded forecast band, guided 7-step tour, share-card canvas, phone bottom nav, installable PWA. Clean and readable; standard dashboard aesthetics.
evidence.physical_or_sensory: none (phone camera receipt scan is the only physical touch)
evidence.integrity_flags: 8 commits with real features (Phase 1 tracker, transaction log, 8 schools) timestamped 09:29-10:47 EDT Sept 19, before the 11:00 hacking start. Supabase publishable key committed (intended public). Claude/Anthropic receipt path exists as dead code despite No Wrapper framing.
evidence.ai_scaffolding_flags: .claude/launch.json only; DEVPOST.md polished. Docs far smaller than code (~6k lines JS).
evidence.novelty_notes: Budget-tracker category, but with several distinctive mechanisms: eating-days calendars from official academic calendars, a bucket model spanning ten schools' plan types, per-place block value learning, Monte Carlo resampling instead of a straight line, and zero-server OCR.
evidence.need_notes: Specific, relatable pain with concrete numbers ($4k/semester, $14.58/block) and anecdotal evidence; plan data sourced with URLs and verified dates.
evidence.wow_moment: Photograph a real thermal receipt on your phone and it logs '1 block + $2.75 FLEX' at the right cafe, then the home screen says 'FLEX: over 99% chance of running out, Nov 6-17'.
evidence.score_rationale: Common category with genuine twists (S1 5). Real student pain with data (S2 7). No Wrapper fit is solid (OCR + Monte Carlo, no LLM shipped) plus .Tech/DO (S3 6). Live, polished, tests, error states, offline (S4 13). Attractive but conventional dashboard, camera scan is the only tactile bit (S5 8). Wow is a mild 'neat'.
evidence.judge_summary: A very complete, live meal-plan tracker for ten schools with on-device receipt OCR and a Monte Carlo run-out forecast. Solid No Wrapper entry; not flashy. Note several feature commits landed ~90 minutes before the official start.

name: Dayfork
one_liner: Describe a two-option decision; Nemotron structures it, a deterministic browser engine computes monthly cost/time, break-even or subscription totals, and Nemotron then writes paired parallel storylines for both paths without picking a winner.
judge_note: Type a two-option decision; Nemotron builds a structured scenario, the browser computes monthly cost/time and break-evens, toggling factors updates numbers instantly, then Nemotron writes paired parallel stories with facts inserted by code. Clean UI, real eval harness, heavily Codex-built, localhost only.
wow_moment: Toggle 'Take an Uber after class' and change 6 to 10 trips: the Far option's monthly cost/time changes instantly, the two parallel stories are flagged stale, and Update Story regenerates aligned Morning/Daytime/Evening narratives with the exact new figures inserted by code.

evidence.one_liner: Describe a two-option decision; Nemotron structures it, a deterministic browser engine computes monthly cost/time, break-even or subscription totals, and Nemotron then writes paired parallel storylines for both paths without picking a winner.
evidence.problem: People weighing medium/long-term two-way decisions (on- vs off-campus housing, gaming vs office laptop, coffee machine vs buying coffee, annual vs monthly membership) struggle to see both paths as lived tradeoffs rather than a spreadsheet.
evidence.target_user: Students and individuals facing a personal two-option decision; generic, no user evidence given.
evidence.core_loop: Textarea decision -> POST /api/scenarios/generate -> Spring GenerationService prompts Nemotron with a JSON schema generated from the frontend validator -> ContractValidator + one bounded repair -> Decision JSON -> zod validation -> BaselineReview numeric editors -> Dashboard runs simulate() in-browser (factor toggles, importance sliders, bar/line/step charts) -> StoryPanel POST /api/stories/generate with frozen snapshot + fact inventory -> Nemotron fills narrative slots -> StoryValidator/StoryDraftAssembler bind IDs and facts -> paired stories rendered with {{fact}} placeholders; edits mark the story stale until Update Story.
evidence.mocked_or_hardcoded: Four fixture decisions (campus housing, laptop, coffee, membership) and an offline story generator (offlineStories.ts) explicitly labeled 'Offline example preview'; backend unit tests mock ModelClient. Live generation requires NVIDIA_API_KEY/NVIDIA_MODEL env vars; without them the app reports 'model not configured' rather than silently swapping in fixtures.
evidence.demo_risks: Hosted NVIDIA API: their own validation docs record 60s provider timeouts (5 of 7 cases timed out in one run; ~13s success after enabling low-effort reasoning). Model JSON can still fail validation after one repair and surface an error. Localhost only (Java 21 + Node 24, Vite proxy). Story generation is slow for a 3-minute demo; offline demos are the safe path.
evidence.ui_experience: Polished light Tailwind UI (Manrope/DM Sans, blue/teal option accents): hero input screen with offline-demo chips, 3-step progress header, baseline review cards with numeric editors, dashboard with factor toggles + importance sliders, recharts bar/line/step charts, 'Trace every number' breakdown sheet (Radix dialog), story panel with paired stage timeline (Beginning/During/Later or Morning/Daytime/Evening), stale badges, loading/error/abort states, aria labels and reduced-motion support. Three screens; text/form heavy but touchable.
evidence.integrity_flags: All 15 commits inside the window (Sep 19 12:57 to Sep 20 05:16 EDT). No secrets (.env.example blank, .env ignored). README ends 'Coworked with Codex'; MEMORY.md says the agent should 'communicate with the user in Chinese' and that the user 'authorized implementation' -- the codebase is essentially agent-built by one person (IvanLiu/2004Moonlove). Originally named 'Parallel Me'; MEMORY.md lists differentiating from a 'SASEHacks ParallelMe project' and 'Wage101 Commute vs Rent', so the concept resembles a prior hackathon project (provenance unclear, no copied code seen). artifacts/ holds screenshots of a 'Clear Choice' app in CNY with a footer link 'Original Dayfork workspace' that does not match this codebase -- unexplained.
evidence.ai_scaffolding_flags: AGENTS.md, 28KB MEMORY.md (project memory/contract for the agent), four dated validation reports in docs/. Docs are not larger than code (~55KB docs vs ~380KB src incl. tests), but the whole workflow is agent-driven.
evidence.novelty_notes: 'Parallel lives for a decision' is a known genre (their own memory cites a prior ParallelMe). The distinctive part is the mechanism: the LLM never does arithmetic; code owns cents/minutes, break-even and subscription math, generates the prompt schema from the frontend validator, validates and repairs once, and inserts facts via placeholders. A careful 'LLM as narrative layer' design rather than a new problem space.
evidence.need_notes: Plausible everyday pain (housing, laptop, gym plan) but no user quotes, data or domain insight; the product explicitly refuses to recommend, which limits the payoff for the user.
evidence.wow_moment: Toggle 'Take an Uber after class' and change 6 to 10 trips: the Far option's monthly cost/time changes instantly, the two parallel stories are flagged stale, and Update Story regenerates aligned Morning/Daytime/Evening narratives with the exact new figures inserted by code.
evidence.score_rationale: Known 'two-path stories' genre, but the mechanism (deterministic engine owns all math, Nemotron only fills narrative slots with fact placeholders, schema generated from the validator, bounded repair, live eval harness with documented failures) is unusually rigorous. Need is generic with no evidence. Strong Beyond-the-Chatbot fit. Wired end to end with 150+ tests and labeled offline fallbacks, but the live path depends on a hosted API that timed out in their own runs. Polished, text-heavy UI.
evidence.judge_summary: Type a two-option decision; Nemotron builds a structured scenario, the browser computes monthly cost/time and break-evens, toggling factors updates numbers instantly, then Nemotron writes paired parallel stories with facts inserted by code. Clean UI, real eval harness, heavily Codex-built, localhost only.

name: Mesh Mail
one_liner: Receive and reply to Gmail over a Meshtastic LoRa mesh with no cellular or Wi-Fi at the far end, using a custom compressed 200-byte packet codec and an off-grid inbox UI.
judge_note: Email squeezed into 200-byte LoRa packets and read on an internet-less laptop through two Meshtastic radios, with replies going back. Genuinely hard, physical, no LLM; rough edges and no phone app yet.
wow_moment: Send yourself an email, watch the gateway laptop chunk it into ~70 bytes, and seconds later it appears in an inbox on an air-gapped laptop wired only to a blinking LoRa radio, then reply back through the mesh.

evidence.one_liner: Receive and reply to Gmail over a Meshtastic LoRa mesh with no cellular or Wi-Fi at the far end, using a custom compressed 200-byte packet codec and an off-grid inbox UI.
evidence.problem: Email is unreachable without internet; LoRa mesh radios can carry tiny packets for miles if mail is shrunk and chunked.
evidence.target_user: People off-grid or in outages (hikers, disaster responders, rural users) who still need email.
stack: zlib raw deflate with shared dictionary
stdlib HTTP server + plain HTML/JS inbox (older Streamlit UI)
LilyGO T-Beam S3 LoRa nodes on stock firmware
evidence.core_loop: MessagePing polls Gmail history -> MessageTransform -> MeshCodec.to_packets strips quotes/URLs, deflates with DICT, chunks to <=200 B with id/part/total header -> MeshSend paced on the radio's real TX queue -> LoRa private channel -> end node -> station.py reassembles, requests missing parts, decodes -> endpoint/server.py JSON API -> web inbox; replies/compose travel back as OUTBOUND packets and MessageReply sends via Gmail.
evidence.mocked_or_hardcoded: MockRadio loopback via a spool folder and a 'demo' transport with sample mail; README status admits the gateway loop joining Gmail to the radio and the phone app are 'not built yet' (MyApplication/ holds only .idea); range untested (nodes side by side); Windows Bluetooth hangs.
evidence.demo_risks: Moderate: needs two T-Beams with antennas on the right region/channel, USB ports, Gmail OAuth on the gateway, ~2 s airtime per packet; loopback/demo modes as fallback.
evidence.ui_experience: Dark glassy Mesh Mail inbox (plain HTML/JS): live-connection pill, transport selector listing real COM ports, threads, compose/reply, real packet-progress bar. Basic but tidy. The radios themselves are the visual.
evidence.integrity_flags: projectContext.txt calls it a firmware fork; README correctly says stock firmware. Commit names 'Betterified the entire codebase', 'The 20 minute prooompt', two 'Revert to state at...' commits suggest LLM rewrites and rollbacks. Secrets (channel.url, secrets.json, tokens) correctly gitignored. Commits start 11:29 after start.
evidence.ai_scaffolding_flags: projectContext.txt is a prompt-context file; commit messages reference prompting. Docs are small relative to ~2.8k lines of code.
evidence.novelty_notes: Email over LoRa mesh is uncommon at hackathons and needs real engineering (dictionary compression, chunk/reassembly, retransmit requests, airtime pacing) with physical radios.
evidence.need_notes: Off-grid comms is a real need (disasters, backcountry), though email specifically is slightly contrived; no evidence or users given.
evidence.wow_moment: Send yourself an email, watch the gateway laptop chunk it into ~70 bytes, and seconds later it appears in an inbox on an air-gapped laptop wired only to a blinking LoRa radio, then reply back through the mesh.
evidence.score_rationale: Uncommon problem with a real mechanism (S1 8). Real but under-evidenced need (S2 5). Strong No Wrapper fit: no LLM, explainably hard, physical demo (S3 7). Codec, radio send, reassembly and reply exist and reportedly ran on hardware, but the README admits gaps and the phone app is absent (S4 9). Physical radios plus a modest web inbox (S5 9).
evidence.judge_summary: Email squeezed into 200-byte LoRa packets and read on an internet-less laptop through two Meshtastic radios, with replies going back. Genuinely hard, physical, no LLM; rough edges and no phone app yet.

name: Heard!
one_liner: An ambient meeting teammate: listens via ElevenLabs Scribe, mints sticky-note cards for ideas with Nemotron, researches open questions with Claude sub-agents, and speaks up through a harness that only lets it talk when asked or when a finding lands.
judge_note: A sticky-note board that listens to the meeting, files ideas as cards, researches them in the background and talks back when asked. Charming and well-evaluated on the Nemotron side; fragile on stage and partly built from a pre-hackathon base.
wow_moment: Say 'Heard, has anyone built this before?' and a few seconds later a card reads 'DONE BEFORE, 9+ times' while the board speaks 'nine Devpost projects do this, plus Be My Eyes...' with a linked research page.

evidence.one_liner: An ambient meeting teammate: listens via ElevenLabs Scribe, mints sticky-note cards for ideas with Nemotron, researches open questions with Claude sub-agents, and speaks up through a harness that only lets it talk when asked or when a finding lands.
evidence.problem: Working meetings lose ideas and threads, and nobody looks things up in the moment ('has anyone built this before?').
evidence.target_user: Small teams in brainstorming/working sessions (hackathon teams, product groups).
stack: Claude Agent SDK (front desk + WebSearch researchers)
ElevenLabs Scribe v2 realtime STT + streamed TTS
evidence.core_loop: Mic -> Scribe v2 -> append-only transcript.md -> Nemotron classifier every 2-5 s (new subject, addressed, questions, salience) -> placeholder card + signal; Nemotron notes agent rewrites notes.md every 20 s -> front desk (Claude Agent SDK) wakes with tools recall/investigate/say/note/working -> sub-agents web-search and write an HTML card page -> harness checks reason (asked/finding), budget, floor -> ElevenLabs TTS -> board over WebSocket.
evidence.mocked_or_hardcoded: fixtures/demo.txt scripted meeting replay and /inject text path for testing; browser STT fallback with nothing spoken when ElevenLabs key absent; research pinned to haiku/low effort; nothing else mocked.

evidence.ui_experience: Paper-theme board: pastel square sticky notes with ruled lines that grow as people talk, a stop-motion sheep flock start screen, Board/Notes/Transcript views, thinking-level switch, investigations rail with timers, and a bottom strip of woke/said/hearing events with a highlighted spoken line. Distinctive, calm, and legible; judges can talk to it.
evidence.physical_or_sensory: audio (live voice in and spoken replies)
evidence.integrity_flags: First commit (23:51 Sept 19) ports 3,867 lines from a prior 'Heard! kitchen build' (STT/TTS, WebSocket hub, config, NIM client, board mic/audio helpers), i.e. roughly 40% of the Python is pre-existing; README discloses Claude Code authorship and commits carry Co-Authored-By. No secrets.
evidence.ai_scaffolding_flags: No CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md; docs/NEMOTRON.md is an eval write-up. Docs smaller than code (~5.4k lines).
evidence.novelty_notes: AI meeting notetakers are crowded (Otter, Granola), but an agent that mints cards live, dispatches research mid-meeting and interjects under a plain-code harness with 'fails toward silence' rules is a distinctive twist.
evidence.need_notes: Relatable, generic pain; no user evidence beyond the scripted demo, though the 'done before, 9+ times' finding is a compelling illustration.
evidence.wow_moment: Say 'Heard, has anyone built this before?' and a few seconds later a card reads 'DONE BEFORE, 9+ times' while the board speaks 'nine Devpost projects do this, plus Be My Eyes...' with a linked research page.
evidence.score_rationale: Crowded category, real twist (S1 6). Plausible but generic need (S2 5). Nails Beyond the Chatbot (clear split, six-config benchmark with latencies and documented failures) and is voice-first with ElevenLabs both ways (S3 8). Working loop with tests and eval, but three fragile services and ~40% ported code, no live URL (S4 11). Attractive, live, audible (S5 10).
evidence.judge_summary: A sticky-note board that listens to the meeting, files ideas as cards, researches them in the background and talks back when asked. Charming and well-evaluated on the Nemotron side; fragile on stage and partly built from a pre-hackathon base.

name: Pyre
one_liner: A bank chat assistant (React Native) whose LLM agent can only read the signed-in customer's data through policy-gated tools, issues server-built dispute and fraud-triage forms instead of acting, and hands cases to a staff review dashboard that credits the account in a Firestore transaction.
judge_note: A bank chatbot that refuses to act: it classifies intent cheaply, reads only your own data, hands you a server-built dispute or fraud form, and routes the case to a staff dashboard that credits the account. Well-engineered, conventional to look at.
wow_moment: Type 'I don't recognize this charge', get a triage card that asks whether you made it, lock the card and open a claim, then flip to the staff dashboard, approve it, and watch the balance credit appear.

evidence.one_liner: A bank chat assistant (React Native) whose LLM agent can only read the signed-in customer's data through policy-gated tools, issues server-built dispute and fraud-triage forms instead of acting, and hands cases to a staff review dashboard that credits the account in a Firestore transaction.
evidence.problem: Disputing a duplicate or unrecognized charge and locking a card is slow and confusing; chatbots that act on money are risky, so the agent should surface and structure, never decide.
evidence.target_user: Retail bank customers (chat app) and bank dispute-review staff (dashboard).
stack: pydantic-ai with Anthropic Claude (haiku router, opus agent)
evidence.core_loop: Message -> regex rules then a tiny Claude Haiku classifier decide scope -> Claude agent with typed tools (accounts, transactions, duplicates, start_dispute_form, start_fraud_triage, dispute status) reading Firestore for the session's user_id -> chat returns prose plus structured cards (dispute form, triage form, case card, suggestions) -> customer submits form -> POST /disputes creates case (irreversible tier, confirmation required); card lock/replace via triage -> staff dashboard lists pending cases, approve/reject/provisional credit -> balance and reversal written transactionally.
evidence.mocked_or_hardcoded: Bank accounts/transactions are synthetic Firestore documents (no seed script in repo). Welcome text promises transfers and bill pay the agent explicitly declines. Server-side keyword lists (DISPUTE_INTENT etc.) backstop the model when it fails to issue a form.
evidence.demo_risks: Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY with credits (chat route surfaces 'out of credits' hints), a Firebase service-account JSON in backend/, Firestore connectivity and Firebase Auth. Opus latency per turn. No README describing the project, tracks or how to run the three apps.
evidence.ui_experience: Chase-styled chat screen (blue palette, app logo, online status, typing indicator, day dividers, grouped bubbles, tool trace, suggestion chips, scroll-to-bottom) with inline dispute/triage form cards; login/signup; a separate staff dashboard with disputes queue, tool policy list and settings. Attractive standard fintech look, no unusual interaction.
evidence.integrity_flags: All 28 commits within the event by 3 contributors. Firebase admin key referenced by filename but not committed. Frontend and dashboard READMEs are untouched Expo/Next templates. Uses Anthropic models, no Nemotron.
evidence.ai_scaffolding_flags: dashboard/CLAUDE.md (@AGENTS.md) and AGENTS.md are the auto-generated Next.js agent rules only. Extensive design-rationale comments in Python suggest AI-assisted authoring; docs are small relative to code.
evidence.novelty_notes: Banking chatbot is a familiar category; the twist is the explicit policy tiers (read / reversible / irreversible + confirmation), server-issued forms, a cheap pre-router, and a human-in-the-loop staff dashboard.
evidence.need_notes: Dispute friction is real but the pitch is generic and undocumented; no evidence or user insight in repo.
evidence.wow_moment: Type 'I don't recognize this charge', get a triage card that asks whether you made it, lock the card and open a claim, then flip to the staff dashboard, approve it, and watch the balance credit appear.
evidence.score_rationale: Solid Compound-track fit with an unusually careful agent safety design across three apps, all wired to Firestore. Held back by a generic chatbot premise, no README or evidence of need, no tests, and full dependence on paid Claude calls during the demo.
evidence.judge_summary: A bank chatbot that refuses to act: it classifies intent cheaply, reads only your own data, hands you a server-built dispute or fraud form, and routes the case to a staff dashboard that credits the account. Well-engineered, conventional to look at.

name: Canopy Co.
one_liner: A pixel-art turn-based game where you run a company in the Amazon; your real stress, read from your webcam via Presage SmartSpectra, shortens your turn timer and makes the greedy, forest-destroying cards more likely to appear.
judge_note: A pixel-art deforestation game where your webcam-measured stress shrinks the clock and stacks the deck with greedy cards. Playable, themed, and physical; the Presage hookup is real with a simulated fallback.
wow_moment: Judge sits down, the stress bar flips from 'simulated' to 'live', and as they hurry their pulse shortens the timer and the land-grab card starts showing up every turn.

evidence.one_liner: A pixel-art turn-based game where you run a company in the Amazon; your real stress, read from your webcam via Presage SmartSpectra, shortens your turn timer and makes the greedy, forest-destroying cards more likely to appear.
evidence.problem: Illustrates how time pressure and stress push decision-makers toward short-term extractive choices; an awareness/education game about deforestation rather than a stated user pain.
evidence.target_user: Players / students; anyone curious how their own physiology changes their choices.
stack: Pixel-art PNG assets + custom TTF font
evidence.core_loop: Story screen -> 18 turns over 3 acts alternating human and bot company -> drawChoices() picks 3 cards weighted by current stress (calm/mid/high tiers) -> choice applies profit/trust/stress/forest deltas -> tile grid greys out as forest health drops -> random events in later acts -> timeout auto-picks the highest-profit card -> ending reveals winner then 'the real number' (hectares lost, panicked decisions). usePresageSocket receives {stress} from bridge.mjs, which maps pulse and breathing rate to 0-100; simulated stress ramp when no bridge.
evidence.mocked_or_hardcoded: Simulated stress fallback runs whenever the bridge is not connected (the label says '(simulated)'). Tile data file is unused; the grid is 120 identical forest tiles. Bot opponent is a heuristic. main.jsx is a leftover diagnostic error-overlay entry point.
evidence.demo_risks: Live path needs a SMARTSPECTRA_API_KEY, a webcam with good lighting and the Node bridge running locally; the SDK also needs network to validate the key. If it fails the game still plays with fake stress, which weakens the pitch. README has no description.
evidence.ui_experience: Full-screen forest photo backdrop, wooden-frame pixel GUI panels, four pixel-art stat bars (profit, trust, stress, forest), a 12x10 tile grid with random tile art that turns grey as the forest dies, choice cards tinted by risk tier, a turn timer, story/event/ending screens with a two-stage reveal. Charming and playable in three minutes.
evidence.integrity_flags: Uses a stock forest PNG and a stock pixel-sky JPG. Vite template README left in place with only team names added. 69 commits from 3 people, all within the event. No secrets.
evidence.ai_scaffolding_flags: .agents/skills/using-smartspectra/SKILL.md and skills-lock.json (Presage-provided SDK skill). No CLAUDE.md.
evidence.novelty_notes: Biofeedback-driven strategy game is a genuinely new mechanism at this event: physiology is a game input that degrades your option set, not just a displayed number.
evidence.need_notes: No user pain; it is an awareness piece. The ending's 'what that actually cost' reveal gives it a point.
evidence.wow_moment: Judge sits down, the stress bar flips from 'simulated' to 'live', and as they hurry their pulse shortens the timer and the land-grab card starts showing up every turn.
evidence.score_rationale: Real Presage SDK integration feeding a working game loop with a clear mechanic and a message; no LLM anywhere. Rough edges (unused data, debug overlay, empty README) and a weak 'need' story, but it is the kind of thing judges can play and feel.
evidence.judge_summary: A pixel-art deforestation game where your webcam-measured stress shrinks the clock and stacks the deck with greedy cards. Playable, themed, and physical; the Presage hookup is real with a simulated fallback.

name: BankManager
one_liner: Enter a ticker; code pulls SEC filings and market data, computes every number, a panel of Claude analyst agents plus a red team interpret them, a verifier checks each claim, and a report says whether the stock beats the S&P 500 over three horizons.
